purpose: Execution of chapters 8, 9 and 11 of the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts (2016 edition): set-off (art. 8.1–8.5), assignment of rights (art. 9.1.1–9.1.15), transfer of obligations (art. 9.2.1–9.2.8), assignment of contracts (art. 9.3.1–9.3.7), plurality of obligors and of obligees (art. 11.1.1–11.2.4). The types for party and contract and the organ come from the hub `unidroit.picc`. The 1980 UN Convention has none of these chapters. The list of questions and boundaries is in analysis/questions.json and QUESTIONS.md.
limitations: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).

THE 1980 UN CONVENTION HAS NEITHER SET-OFF NOR ASSIGNMENT NOR SOLIDARITY AT ALL: its subject is the formation of a contract for the international sale of goods and the rights of the parties under it. There is no bridge to `intl.uncitral.cisg*` here in substance, not for want of work; the way to these chapters is opened by article 7(2) of the Convention.

SPECIAL RULES ON NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS AND ON THE TRANSFER OF A BUSINESS ARE EXCLUDED BY THE SOURCE ITSELF (articles 9.1.2, 9.2.2, 9.3.2): their conditions are a question of the applicable law and an input of the case.

THE MODEL DOES NOT COMPUTE SHARES AND AMOUNTS: articles 8.5, 11.1.9–11.1.13 and 11.2.4 name the rule (to the extent of the lesser obligation, in equal shares, proportionally), while the numbers are brought by the case. Proportional imputation of a set-off (article 8.4(2)) is declared rather than computed for the same reason.

AN EXCLUSIVELY PERSONAL CHARACTER OF AN OBLIGATION (articles 9.1.7, 9.2.6) AND A SIGNIFICANTLY MORE BURDENSOME OBLIGATION CAUSED BY AN ASSIGNMENT (articles 9.1.3, 9.1.4) ARE FACTS OF THE CASE: both assessments are brought by the case, not derived by the model.

SOLIDARITY IS PRESUMED (article 11.1.2), AND THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE REBUT IT. The source does not enumerate which circumstances indicate separate obligations — that is an assertion of the case.
